sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (December 1997), 238 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 1 'Special Relativity and Flat Spacetime' printed pp. 3-28 (PDF pp. 10-35): the metric, Lorentz transformations, the light cone, vectors, dual vectors, tensors, index manipulation, worldlines, proper time, four-velocity and four-momentum. Ch. 2 'Manifolds' printed pp. 44-51 (PDF pp. 51-58): vectors as derivatives, coordinate bases, the tensor transformation law, partial derivatives are not tensors, the metric again, canonical form of the metric, Riemann normal coordinates. Ch. 3 'Curvature' printed pp. 88-92 (PDF pp. 95-99): tetrads and non-coordinate bases. Ch. 4 'Gravitation' printed pp. 97-113 (PDF pp. 104-120): the principle of equivalence, physics in curved spacetime and energy-momentum.

contents.name: Ch. 1 'the metric' and 'Lorentz transformations' with the Lorentz factor (printed pp. 4-6, PDF pp. 11-13)
contents.support: The metric, the Lorentz factor normalization and the transformation of frame components are the lecture-notes setting adopted by the observer, projection and relative-velocity items.

contents.name: Ch. 1 'the light cone' and the causal classification of vectors (printed pp. 7 and 15-16, PDF pp. 14 and 22-23)
contents.support: The light-cone picture and the sign classification of vectors as timelike, lightlike or spacelike back the future/past criterion proved in the pairing lemma.

contents.name: Ch. 1 'vectors', 'dual vectors', 'tensors' and 'tensor products' (printed pp. 8-15, PDF pp. 15-22)
contents.support: The component formalism and the tensor action on dual vectors are restated in the definition of type (r,s) tensor fields and their components.

contents.name: Ch. 1 'index manipulation': contraction over one upper and one lower index, raising and lowering (printed pp. 17-19, PDF pp. 24-26)
contents.support: The contraction operation and the index conventions of the lecture notes are the ones made precise and proved smooth in the contraction lemma.

contents.name: Ch. 1 'worldlines' and 'proper time' (printed pp. 25-26, PDF pp. 32-33)
contents.support: Parametrized worldlines and the four-velocity field along them motivate the congruence definition; no conglomerate of curves is identified with a single observer.

contents.name: Ch. 1 'four-velocity' and 'energy-momentum vector' (1.98)-(1.102) (printed pp. 26-28, PDF pp. 33-35)
contents.support: U^mu = dx^mu/dtau, its normalization, p^mu = mU^mu and the energy component are the lecture-notes source of the observer energy and rest-mass definitions.

contents.name: Ch. 1 'energy-momentum tensor', 'perfect fluids' and 'energy-momentum conservation' (printed pp. 28-31, PDF pp. 35-38)
contents.reason: The stress-energy tensor of continuous matter and its conservation law are the matter branch of the Einstein-and-matter page; the tensors page fixes only the tensor slot and the observer split.

contents.name: Ch. 2 'vectors as derivatives', 'coordinate bases', 'the tensor transformation law' and 'partial derivatives are not tensors' (printed pp. 44-47, PDF pp. 51-54)
contents.support: The chain-rule derivation of the component transformation law and the warning that partial derivatives are not tensors are the lecture-notes version of the transformation lemma.

contents.name: Ch. 2 'the metric again' and 'canonical form of the metric' (printed pp. 47-50, PDF pp. 54-57)
contents.support: Orthogonal complements and the canonical form of the metric in an orthonormal basis are used in the proof that the observer rest space is positive definite.

contents.name: Ch. 2 'Riemann normal coordinates' (printed pp. 50-51, PDF pp. 57-58)
contents.reason: Riemann normal coordinates and momentarily comoving frames belong to the connection and free-fall page, which constructs the metric connection; the tensors page defines frames without normal coordinates.

contents.name: Ch. 3 'tetrads and non-coordinate bases': vielbeins and orthonormal-frame components (printed pp. 88-91, PDF pp. 95-98)
contents.support: The tetrad (vielbein) field with g_mu nu e^mu_a e^nu_b = eta_ab is the lecture-notes source of the tetrad-field definition and its future-directed refinements.

contents.name: Ch. 3 'the spin connection', 'Maurer-Cartan structure equations', 'fiber bundles and gauge transformations' (printed pp. 92-96, PDF pp. 99-103)
contents.reason: The spin connection and the Maurer-Cartan equations belong to the principal-bundle formalism that this track does not develop; the page uses only the local tetrad field, not parallel transport in a frame bundle.

contents.name: Ch. 4 'the principle of equivalence' and 'gravitation as spacetime curvature' (printed pp. 97-103, PDF pp. 104-110)
contents.reason: The equivalence principle and the Newtonian-limit material are the subject of the flat and Newtonian bridges page; nothing on the tensors page depends on them.

contents.name: Ch. 4 'physics in curved spacetime' and 'energy-momentum conservation' (printed pp. 104-113, PDF pp. 111-120)
contents.reason: How physical laws are transcribed to curved spacetime and the conservation law are the Einstein-and-matter page's content; the observer items here use only kinematics, not field equations.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), 126 PDF pages
sources.locator: Sections 1.6-1.10 printed pp. 15-23 (PDF pp. 16-24): abstract index notation, tensors, tensor fields, integral curves and the commutator. Sections 2.1-2.3 printed pp. 24-31 (PDF pp. 25-32): the metric, Lorentzian signature with orthonormal bases and the causal classification, proper time and the 4-velocity. Section 6.3 printed pp. 63-67 (PDF pp. 64-68): the energy-momentum tensor, 4-momentum, rest mass and observer energy.

contents.name: Sections 1.7-1.8 on tensors, tensor fields, components in a basis and the change of coordinate bases (printed pp. 16-21, PDF pp. 17-22)
contents.support: The abstract-index and component definitions of tensor fields and their transformation between bases are the second independent treatment of the tensor-field definition.

contents.name: Section 1.9 on integral curves: definition and the unique integral curve through each point (printed pp. 21-22, PDF pp. 22-23)
contents.support: The existence and uniqueness of the integral curve through each point of a smooth field is what makes the observer curves of a congruence well defined.

contents.name: Section 1.10 on the commutator of vector fields (printed p. 22, PDF p. 23)
contents.support: The commutator is the operation behind the necessary commuting condition that distinguishes coordinate frames, stated in the frame definition.

contents.name: Section 2.1 on the metric and the definition of norm and angle (printed p. 24, PDF p. 25)
contents.support: The scalar product is the bilinear form whose restriction to the observer rest space the projection lemma proves positive definite.

contents.name: Section 2.2 Lorentzian signature: orthonormal bases at a point, Lorentz transformations between them and the causal classification with its two disconnected sets (printed pp. 26-28, PDF pp. 27-29)
contents.support: The statement that different orthonormal bases are related exactly by Lorentz transformations (2.9)-(2.10) is the lecture-notes source of the tetrad-change lemma.

contents.name: Section 2.3 on proper time and the 4-velocity with the normalization g_ab u^a u^b = -1 (2.14) (printed pp. 28-31, PDF pp. 29-32)
contents.support: The unit-timelike normalization of the 4-velocity is the normalization hypothesis of the relative-velocity decomposition theorem.

contents.name: Section 2.3 on the Euler-Lagrange derivation of geodesics and the Christoffel symbols (2.24)-(2.25) (printed pp. 30-31, PDF pp. 31-32)
contents.reason: The geodesic equation and the Christoffel symbols belong to the connection and free-fall page, which owns the metric-selected connection; this page never differentiates a field.

contents.name: Section 6.3 on P = m u, g(P,P) = -m^2 and the observer energy E = -g_ab(p) v^a(p) P^b(p) (6.17)-(6.19) (printed pp. 63-67, PDF pp. 64-68)
contents.support: The 4-momentum normalization and the observer-energy pairing are the second independent treatment behind the energy, momentum and mass-shell identities.

contents.name: Sections 6.3-6.4 on continuous matter and Einstein's equation (printed pp. 65-70, PDF pp. 66-71)
contents.reason: The stress-energy of matter and the field equation are the Einstein-and-matter page's topic; the tensors page defines observer-relative quantities for a single tangent vector only.

sources.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), 290 PDF pages
sources.locator: Sections 2.2.2-2.3.3 printed pp. 62-75 (PDF pp. 69-82): vector fields, integral curves, the Lie derivative, covectors and tensors and tensor fields. Sections 3.1.2-3.1.3 printed pp. 93-95 (PDF pp. 100-102): Lorentzian manifolds, the causal classification and light cone, the metric isomorphism and the inverse metric.

contents.name: Sections 2.2.2-2.2.3 on vector fields and integral curves (printed pp. 62-64, PDF pp. 69-71)
contents.support: The definition of a vector field and of the integral curve through each point is the third treatment backing the observer-curve part of the congruence definition.

contents.name: Section 2.2.4 on the Lie derivative of tensors (printed pp. 65-68, PDF pp. 72-75)
contents.reason: The Lie derivative of general tensor fields is the imported smooth-manifolds library's content and is used on the connection and curvature pages, not here.

contents.name: Sections 2.3.1-2.3.2 on covectors, one-forms and the Lie derivative revisited (printed pp. 69-71, PDF pp. 76-78)
contents.support: Covectors and one-forms are the type (0,1) case of the type (r,s) tensor fields defined on this page; the cotangent basis supplies the component slots.

contents.name: Section 2.3.3 on tensors and tensor fields (printed pp. 72-75, PDF pp. 79-82)
contents.support: The component transformation rules and the tensor-field definition are the lecture-notes version restated by the type (r,s) definition and the transformation lemma.

contents.name: Sections 2.4.1-2.4.5 on differential forms, the exterior derivative, integration and Stokes' theorem (printed pp. 77-90, PDF pp. 84-97)
contents.reason: Differential forms and the exterior derivative are the imported exterior-calculus supplier's content; this page consumes its alpha wedge d alpha criterion only through the cited Frobenius corollary.

contents.name: Sections 3.1.1-3.1.2 on Riemannian and Lorentzian manifolds, timelike, null and spacelike vectors and the light cone (printed pp. 92-93, PDF pp. 99-100)
contents.support: The Lorentzian manifold with its causal classification and light cone is the third independent treatment of the arena in which observers are defined.

contents.name: Section 3.1.3 on the metric isomorphism, the inverse metric and the volume form (printed pp. 94-95, PDF pp. 101-102)
contents.support: The metric isomorphism and the inverse metric underlie the flat map and the index conventions used in the projection identity.

sources.title: J. M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed. (Springer GTM 218, 2013), 708 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 8 'Vector Fields' printed pp. 174-199: vector fields and Lie brackets (pp. 185-189). Ch. 9 'Integral Curves and Flows' printed pp. 205-245: integral curves, flows, flowouts and commuting vector fields (pp. 206-235). Ch. 12 'Tensors' printed pp. 304-324: multilinear algebra, symmetric and alternating tensors, tensors and tensor fields on manifolds (pp. 305-324). Ch. 19 'Distributions and Foliations' printed pp. 490-512: distributions and involutivity (pp. 491-496), the Frobenius theorem (pp. 496-501) and foliations (pp. 501-505).

contents.name: Ch. 8 'Vector Fields on Manifolds' and 'Lie Brackets' (printed pp. 174-189)
contents.support: The Lie bracket and the example that coordinate vector fields commute are the textbook source of the necessary commuting condition for a coordinate frame.

contents.name: Ch. 9 'Integral Curves', 'Flows' and 'Flowouts' with the canonical form of a flow (printed pp. 206-224)
contents.support: The flow box theorem (canonical form of a flow) is the textbook result applied to the congruence field to produce a local adapted chart.

contents.name: Ch. 9 'Commuting Vector Fields' (printed pp. 231-235)
contents.support: Commuting independent vector fields are exactly the coordinate fields of a chart, the converse direction of the commuting condition quoted by the frame definition.

contents.name: Ch. 12 'Multilinear Algebra' and 'Tensors and Tensor Fields on Manifolds' (printed pp. 305-324)
contents.support: The multilinear-algebra definition of tensors, contraction and the tensor-bundle formulation of tensor fields are the textbook source scaffolded by the type (r,s) definition and the contraction lemma.

contents.name: Ch. 19 'Distributions and Involutivity' and 'The Frobenius Theorem' (printed pp. 491-501)
contents.support: The theory of smooth distributions, involutivity and the Frobenius local coordinate theorem is the textbook source of the integrability criterion for the rest spaces.

contents.name: Ch. 19 'Foliations' (printed pp. 501-505)
contents.reason: The global foliation theory of Lee Ch. 19 'Foliations' is developed by the imported distributions-and-integral-manifolds supplier; this page consumes only the local coordinate theorem.

sources.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035v1 (2007), 221 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 2 'Geometry of hypersurfaces' printed pp. 15-37: framework and notations (pp. 15-18), hypersurfaces, normal vector, intrinsic and extrinsic curvature and the Weingarten map (pp. 19-28), spacelike hypersurfaces and the orthogonal projector (pp. 28-34). Ch. 3 'Geometry of foliations' printed pp. 39-49: foliations, lapse, normal evolution vector and Eulerian observers (pp. 39-46). Ch. 4 section 4.2 'Coordinates adapted to the foliation' printed pp. 54-59. Ch. 5 section 5.3 'Perfect fluid' printed pp. 71-79: Lorentz factor and relative velocity of a fluid with respect to the Eulerian observer.

contents.name: Ch. 2 sections 2.3-2.4: hypersurfaces, the normal vector, the Weingarten map and the Frobenius-theorem tangency of the commutator of tangent vectors (printed pp. 19-28)
contents.support: The treatment of a hypersurface by its unit normal and the use of Frobenius' theorem for hypersurface-orthogonality is the monograph's version of the integrability criterion for ker(alpha).

contents.name: Ch. 2 section 2.4.1: the orthogonal decomposition T_pM = T_p(Sigma) + Vect(n) and the orthogonal projector gamma(v) = v + (n.v)n (2.60)-(2.64) (printed pp. 29-31)
contents.support: The projector formula gamma(v) = v + (n.v)n with gamma(n) = 0 and gamma = identity on the tangent space is exactly the spatial projection of an observer, here proved for a hypersurface normal.

contents.name: Ch. 3 sections 3.3.3-3.3.4: Eulerian observers, the lapse, and the remark that a hypersurface-orthogonal congruence has vanishing vorticity (printed pp. 42-44)
contents.support: The statement that hypersurface-orthogonal congruences have vanishing vorticity is the monograph's form of the obstruction that the shearing congruence violates, so its rest spaces admit no local hypersurfaces.

contents.name: Ch. 4 section 4.2: coordinates adapted to the foliation, with x^0 = const. on the leaves (printed pp. 54-59)
contents.support: The construction of coordinates adapted to a foliation is the monograph's treatment of the adapted-chart existence proved here for an observer congruence.

contents.name: Ch. 5 section 5.3: the relative velocity U of a fluid with respect to the Eulerian observer, u = Gamma(n+U) with n.U = 0 and Gamma = (1 - U.U)^-1/2 (5.29)-(5.36) (printed pp. 76-79)
contents.support: The orthogonal decomposition u = Gamma(n+U) of a 4-velocity with respect to an observer and the Lorentz-factor formula are the monograph's version of the relative-velocity decomposition theorem.

contents.name: Ch. 6-12 on evolution systems, initial data, asymptotics and the Cauchy problem (printed pp. 81-221)
contents.reason: The numerical-evolution, initial-data and asymptotics chapters belong to the causal and initial-value pages of the track; the tensors-and-observers pair needs only the projector, foliation and relative-velocity sections read above.
